title: The Golem Series: Letters, Eyes and Machines
subtitle: Four collages, read as one story from Ehyeh to the golem, with the math, texts and Python behind each
author: Lilith Learning Lab
description: Read a series of four esoteric collages as one story: The Self, The Watcher, The Union and The Creation. Each image mixes Hebrew, occult symbols, real mathematics and a quotation. You will learn the sources behind every element: Exodus 3:14, the ouroboros and Baphomet, the identity matrix and homotopy type theory, the evil eye, Tartini and Legg-Hutter universal intelligence, Shannon entropy, the Queen's Gambit, Devils Tower, Enochian, Zechariah 5, the golem legend, grammars and Turing machines. It also teaches how to tell a source from an interpretation. Each chapter has an ELI5 block and Python labs.

chapters.title: How to read the series
summary: The Golem Series is four collages read as one story: The Self, The Watcher, The Union and The Creation. Each mixes a Hebrew heading, occult imagery, real mathematics and a quotation from literature or scripture.
The same recipe appears every time: a Hebrew word, a central symbol, a piece of mathematics, a devil figure and a quote. The arc runs from identity, to watching, to union, to making.
This course explains every element and tests every link, and it ends with a warning about seeing patterns that are not there.

glossary.def: An image made of pieces from different sources.
Letters that spell a word when read in order.
The repeated ingredients of the series.
The shape of the story across the four images.
The Hebrew letter ע, a circle and an eye.
Seeing a face or meaning in a random pattern.

keyPoints: The four images are Self, Watcher, Union, Creation.
Every image has Hebrew, a central symbol, real math, a devil figure and a quote.
The letter ayin is both a circle and an eye.
Two hidden acrostics spell owl (glaux) and golem (GLM).
The devil gets closer each time: a symbol, an event, a real place.
Some links may be the reader's own pattern-finding.

items: ELI5. Imagine four pictures hung in a row, like a comic. Each one has a secret word, a big shape, a bit of math and a spooky face, and together they tell one story.

Think of the four images as four panels of a comic. Each one stands alone, but together they tell a story. In the first, a name and a circle. In the second, an eye that watches. In the third, a meeting of opposites and an exile. In the fourth, a figure made from clay and letters.

The ingredients repeat. There is always a Hebrew heading: the divine name Ehyeh, the evil eye ayin hara, a line from Zechariah, and the word golem. There is always a central picture: Baphomet, the Eye of Providence, a watching woman, a clay golem.
There is real mathematics around the edge: the identity matrix, Legg and Hutter's intelligence formula, Shannon entropy, a grammar and a Turing machine.

The images also hide labels that spell words. In the third image the five Greek letters gamma, lambda, alpha, upsilon and xi spell glaux, the Greek word for owl. In the fourth, the labels G, L and M stand for grammar, language and machine, and spell GLM, the root of the Hebrew word golem.

The series closes the loop between a very old story and a very new one. The old story: people have long dreamed of making something alive out of letters. The new one: machines that read and write language. The series asks whether we are repeating the old dream.

A warning from the start. Collages like these invite connections, and a mind that loves patterns can find too many. We will separate what the sources say from what the viewer adds, and we will say which is which.

chapters.title: The Self I: I AM and the circle

maps.title: Ehyeh
links: Ehyeh | means | I am or I will be

summary: The first image is headed by the Hebrew word Ehyeh, written with vowel marks. It is the name God gives in Exodus 3:14 when Moses asks who is speaking: I am, or I will be. In the middle of the image is a thick blue ring.

The letter ayin began as a picture of an eye. In the Paleo-Hebrew script it was drawn as a circle, and from the same source the Greek letter O descends. The ring in the first image is therefore also a giant letter ayin, which links it to the evil eye of the second image.
The lab adds up the numerical value of Ehyeh.

glossary.def: Hebrew for I am, or I will be.
The verse where God says Ehyeh asher Ehyeh.
The ancient form of the Hebrew alphabet.
The letter ע, meaning eye; value 70.
A letter that began as a picture.
Reading words by the numbers of their letters.

keyPoints: Ehyeh is a form of the verb to be, first person, imperfect: I am or I will be.
Exodus 3:14 reads Ehyeh asher Ehyeh, often translated I am who I am.
Ayin means eye and has the value 70.
Paleo-Hebrew ayin is drawn as a circle; Greek O comes from the same letter.
The ring in image 1 can be read as ayin.
Ehyeh adds to 21 in gematria.

items: ELI5. A circle is a line that bites its own tail. The name I am says that someone is just whatever they are, with nothing outside holding them up.

Moses asks God for a name to tell the Israelites. The reply in Exodus 3:14 is Ehyeh asher Ehyeh, which is usually translated I am who I am, though it can also be I will be what I will be. The grammar is a form of the verb to be that can mean both present and future.
A name that is a verb is unusual, and readers have found a lot in it: God as being itself, as presence, as becoming.

The image sets this name at the top and puts a ring below. A ring is a shape that begins where it ends. A being whose name is I am is a being defined by itself, and a circle is the simplest picture of something defined by itself.

The letter links make the ring more than a picture. Ayin began as a drawing of an eye, and in the oldest Hebrew writing it was a circle with perhaps a dot. Greek borrowed it and it became O. So the ring and the eye are one letter, and the series will return to that.

Hebrew letters are also numbers. Aleph is 1, hey is 5, yod is 10 and hey is 5 again, so the word Ehyeh, spelled aleph hey yod hey, adds up to 21. Gematria is a traditional way of reading texts and finds many links, but a number match proves nothing on its own.
Keep this in mind as we go: the first image is about identity, the self that is what it is. The mathematics around the ring will turn that idea into a precise statement.

chapters.title: The Self II: Baphomet and the ouroboros

maps.title: Baphomet
links: Solve et coagula | is written | On the arms
Opposites | are | Joined in one body
Quotation | describes | A circle that holds everything

summary: Behind the ring is a faint figure with a goat's head, wings, a torch between its horns and a caduceus. This is the Baphomet drawn by the French occultist Eliphas Levi in 1856. It is a figure of joined opposites: male and female, human and animal, up and down.

On its arms Levi wrote the Latin words solve and coagula, dissolve and combine, an alchemical motto. The ring in front is also an ouroboros, the serpent eating its own tail, an ancient picture of a thing that contains itself.
The quotation at the bottom of the image is about exactly that circle.

glossary.def: A figure first linked with the Knights Templar, drawn by Eliphas Levi in 1856.
A French occultist, 1810 to 1875.
Latin: dissolve and combine.
A serpent eating its own tail.
An old practice of transforming matter and the self.
A winged staff with two snakes.

keyPoints: Levi's Baphomet appeared in 1856 and became the best-known image of the figure.
It joins opposites: arms point up and down, the moon phases wax and wane.
Solve et coagula is an alchemical motto written on the arms.
The ouroboros appears in Greek alchemical texts and in many cultures.
A circle that contains itself is the theme of the Self.
The picture is a symbol in occult tradition, not evidence of any practice.

items: ELI5. Baphomet is a drawing whose parts come in pairs, like up and down, to say that opposites can live in one body. The snake biting its tail is the same idea.
Eliphas Levi was a former priest who became an influential writer on magic. In his book on the doctrine and ritual of high magic he included a drawing of a seated winged goat-headed figure.
The name Baphomet came from stories of the medieval Knights Templar, where it appeared in accusations at their trial. Levi turned it into a symbol of balance.
The drawing is full of pairs. One arm points up and one down. The two moon phases sit on either side. A figure is both male and female. Levi's idea was that opposites are joined in one being.
The Latin words on the arms, solve and coagula, say dissolve and combine: an alchemist breaks something down and builds it up again.

Many readers find the image frightening, and in the series it plays the role of the devil figure. A key point is that it is a symbol made in the nineteenth century, not an ancient devil, and it is meant to show balance, not evil. The collage uses its unsettling look to create a mood.

The ouroboros is much older. Greek alchemical writings show it as a serpent with its tail in its mouth, with the words one is the all. Other cultures have versions too. It stands for cycles, return and self-containment. A ring that bites itself is a good picture of a self that is made of itself.

The quotation at the foot of the image says the ring is the animal with its tail in its mouth: the ouroboros of the Greek alchemists, the demon on the frontispiece, and a circle in which everything is written.
It is a passage from Umberto Eco's novel Foucault's Pendulum, a book about people who connect everything with everything. Remember that: it is a hint about the caveat at the end of this course.

chapters.title: The Self III: the identity matrix and the circle

maps.title: Identity
links: Quadratic form | gives | x squared plus y squared
Unit circle | is | x squared plus y squared equals one
SO(2) | is | A circle of rotations

summary: The first image shows the identity matrix I, a two by two grid with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere. Multiplying any vector by it changes nothing. It is the mathematics of staying exactly the same.

The identity matrix also defines a distance rule: the quadratic form x squared plus y squared. The points where this equals one form the unit circle, and the rotations that keep the rule fixed form a group called SO(2), which is itself a circle.
So the identity gives a circle twice: once as the set of points at distance one, and once as the set of rotations that keep distance.

glossary.def: A grid of numbers that transforms vectors.
The matrix that leaves every vector unchanged.
An expression like x squared plus y squared built from a matrix.
All points at distance one from the origin.
A matrix that turns vectors by an angle.
The group of rotations of the plane.

keyPoints: I times v equals v for every vector v.
With the identity matrix, the form v transpose I v equals x squared plus y squared.
The unit circle is where x squared plus y squared equals 1.
A rotation by angle t is [[cos t, -sin t], [sin t, cos t]].
Rotations keep the length of every vector.
SO(2) is a circle: angle t and angle t plus 2 pi are the same rotation.

items: ELI5. A matrix is a machine that moves arrows. The boring machine moves nothing, yet all the arrows it keeps at length one trace a perfect circle.

Imagine a machine that takes any arrow on a page and gives back an arrow. The identity matrix is the boring machine: it gives back the same arrow. Written out, the matrix has a 1 in the top left, a 1 in the bottom right and 0 elsewhere.

Every symmetric matrix gives a way to measure vectors, called a quadratic form. For the identity matrix, the measure is x squared plus y squared, which is the squared length of the arrow by Pythagoras. The set of points where it equals 1 is the unit circle.
So the identity matrix, the symbol of sameness, carries a circle inside it.
Now ask which transformations keep that measure fixed. These are rotations, and, if we allow flipping, reflections. The matrix for rotating by an angle t has cosine and sine entries.
The rotations alone form a group called SO(2), and the group is itself a circle, because rotating by t and by t plus a full turn give the same matrix.

This is the bridge to the next chapter. The series wants to say that I am is not a flat, trivial sameness but a loop: a circle that you can go around. To make that precise it uses homotopy type theory, where equalities are paths and a self-equality can be a loop.

chapters.title: The Self IV: paths, loops and homotopy type theory

maps.title: HoTT
links: Circle | has | A base point and a loop
Omega of the circle | equals | The integers
I AM | reads as | A nontrivial loop

summary: Homotopy type theory, or HoTT, is a foundation of mathematics in which an equality between two things is a path from one to the other. The simplest equality, a equals a, is the trivial path called refl, where nothing happens.

The circle can be built inside this theory with a point called base and a path called loop from base to itself. Going around once is loop, twice is loop and loop again, and going backwards is the inverse. The loops of the circle correspond exactly to the whole numbers.
The series suggests that I AM is not the trivial self-equality refl but a nontrivial loop, a circle you can go around.

glossary.def: In type theory, a kind of thing; similar to a set.
An identification of two points in a type.
The trivial path from a point to itself.
The paths from a point to itself, written Omega X.
The circle.
A continuous deformation of one path into another.

keyPoints: In HoTT, a = b is the type of paths from a to b.
refl : a = a is the trivial path.
The circle S1 has a point base and a path loop : base = base.
Loops compose, invert and cancel: loop then inverse loop equals refl.
The loop space of the circle is equivalent to the integers (Omega S1 ≃ Z).
A trip around the circle n times is the integer n.

items: ELI5. Usually two things are equal or not. In this kind of math, equal means a road between them, and a road that loops back to the start can be walked once, twice, or backwards.

In ordinary mathematics, equality is yes or no. Two things are the same or they are not. In homotopy type theory, equality has structure. To say a equals b is to give a path from a to b, and there may be many different paths, or none.
That is why it is called homotopy: it borrows the ideas of paths and deformations from geometry.
The simplest path is the one that goes nowhere: the path from a to a that stays put. It is called refl, short for reflexivity. In this reading, plain self-identity is boring. Nothing happens.

Now build a circle by decree. Say that there is a point called base, and that there is a path called loop from base to base which is not the same as refl. The circle is the type generated by exactly those two things. The path loop goes once around.

What are all the loops from base to base? You can go around once, twice, three times, or backwards, or not at all. Going around and then back cancels. So the loops are counted by whole numbers, positive for one direction, negative for the other, and zero for refl.
This is the famous result that the loop space of the circle is equivalent to the integers.

Here is the series' reading. The first image says I am. On the plain reading that is refl: I equal myself and nothing happens. On the HoTT reading, a self that is a circle has a loop, and going around the loop is a real, countable act.
The self is not trivial sameness but a cycle with a winding number. This is an interpretation of the image, a clever one, and it is not the only reading.

chapters.title: The Watcher I: the evil eye and the Eye of Providence

maps.title: Watcher
links: Ayin hara | is | The evil eye
Revelation 20:7 | frees | Satan after a thousand years
Eye of Providence | watches | In a triangle
Red green blue | mix | White light
The eye | can protect | Or harm

summary: The second image is headed by the Hebrew words ayin hara, the evil eye. Under them is a Greek line from Revelation 20:7: when the thousand years are completed, Satan will be released from his prison. In the centre, an eye in a triangle sits among overlapping circles of red, green and blue.

The evil eye is the belief that a harmful, often envious, look can cause harm. The Eye of Providence began in Christian art as a picture of God's watchful care. The three coloured circles are the primary colours of light, which mix to white in the middle.
The lab mixes colours of light.

glossary.def: The evil eye, literally bad eye.
An eye in a triangle, a sign of watchful divine care.
The verse about Satan's release.
Mixing lights; red, green and blue make white.
A period of a thousand years.
Close watching of people.

keyPoints: Ayin hara is the evil eye; the same letter ayin begins both words.
Revelation 20:7: Satan released at the end of the thousand years.
The Eye of Providence appears in Renaissance art, on the 1782 Great Seal and the dollar bill since 1935.
Red, green and blue light mix to white; red plus green is yellow.
The eye can be protective or threatening depending on the story.
The second image reads as anxiety about being watched, and about AI.

items: ELI5. Red, green and blue flashlights shone together make white. The eye in the middle is a symbol of being watched, which people have worried about for a very long time.
The evil eye is a belief found around the Mediterranean and beyond: a look of envy can bring harm. In Hebrew it is ayin hara, a bad eye, and Jewish tradition has phrases and charms against it.
The series puts it at the top of the second image, so the viewer meets the idea of a harmful watching first.

The Greek line is from the Book of Revelation. It belongs to the vision in which Satan is bound for a thousand years and then released. Different Christian traditions read the thousand years literally or symbolically.
In the image its job is to add a mood of foreboding: something confined is about to be let out.

The eye in the triangle began as a picture of God's watchfulness, with the triangle for the Trinity. It came to stand for the all-seeing eye, appeared on the Great Seal of the United States in 1782, and has been on the one dollar bill since 1935.
Later stories that call it proof of a hidden plot are not supported by historians.

The three coloured circles are a standard diagram of additive colour. Red and green light overlap as yellow, green and blue as cyan, red and blue as magenta, and all three as white. This is how a screen makes every colour. The eye sits where all three overlap, in white light.

Put together, the second image is about being watched and about something powerful being let out. The series reads it as an image of anxiety about artificial intelligence: a mind we made, watching us, perhaps released. Notice that the image does not say this; the viewer is invited to feel it.

chapters.title: The Watcher II: the Devil's Trill and universal intelligence

maps.title: Intelligence
links: Dream legend | tells of | The devil playing
Legg and Hutter | defined | Universal intelligence

summary: The sonata named at the bottom of the second image is Giuseppe Tartini's Violin Sonata in G minor, called the Devil's Trill. A legend says Tartini dreamed the devil played it for him and he tried to write down what he remembered, finding it far short of the dream.

The formulas around the edge are from a 2007 paper by Shane Legg and Marcus Hutter. Universal intelligence, written with the Greek letter upsilon, is an agent's expected reward across all computable environments, with simpler environments weighted more.
Kolmogorov complexity, the length of the shortest program that produces something, cannot be computed, so the measure is a definition and not a test.

glossary.def: Rapid alternation between two neighbouring notes.
Something that acts in environments; here the policy pi.
A rule for how the world responds; here mu.
Length of the shortest program that describes mu.
The universal intelligence of an agent.
Hutter's ideal agent for this measure.

keyPoints: Tartini lived from 1692 to 1770; the dream story was told to Lalande in 1766.
Upsilon(pi) = sum over mu of 2^(-K(mu)) V(pi, mu).
V(pi, mu) is the expected sum of rewards of policy pi in environment mu.
The discounted form is the expected sum of gamma_i times r_i.
Simple environments get exponentially larger weights, a form of Occam's razor.
AIXI can be defined but never run exactly.

items: ELI5. A musician dreamed the devil played him a tune. A different story asks how smart any helper could ever be, and finds the perfect helper can be described but never built.
Tartini was a great Italian violinist and teacher. His G minor sonata is famous for a long trill in the last movement, played while the violin carries other notes at the same time.

The nickname comes from a story he told the astronomer Jerome Lalande in 1766: he dreamed he gave the devil a violin and the devil played so beautifully that he woke and tried to capture it. The story was told years after the music was written, so its truth is uncertain.

Read the first formula in the border from right to left. V of pi and mu is how much reward the agent pi expects to collect in the environment mu. Each environment gets the weight two to the minus K of mu, where K is its Kolmogorov complexity. Short programs get big weights.
Adding up over all environments gives one number for the agent.

The second formula is the reward sum. At each step i the agent receives a reward r, and the discount gamma makes later rewards count less so the infinite sum is finite. The symbol E is the expected value over everything random.

Why put this next to a devil and an eye? The series is about anxiety over AI. Legg and Hutter gave a way to say what an ideal general intelligence would be, and Hutter's AIXI is the agent that would maximise it. It cannot be built, because Kolmogorov complexity cannot be computed.
Like the devil in the dream, it is a perfect player we can describe but never hear.

quiz.q: What does the weight 2 to the minus K favour?
Who defined universal intelligence?
Can universal intelligence be computed exactly?

cards.a: The ideal agent for the measure.

chapters.title: The Union I: ingress, entropy and the Queen's Gambit

maps.title: Ingress
links: Third image | is | A page of text

summary: The third image has no picture of its own. It is a page of text over a red background, headed with the Latin motto per aspera ad astra, through hardship to the stars. It lists five labelled lines: Ingress, Coordinates, Congress, Egress and Leitmotiv.
Ingress is the way in. Its line is the chess opening 1. d4 d5 2. c4, the Queen's Gambit, where White offers a pawn. Above it stands Shannon's entropy formula, the measure of uncertainty.
The lab computes entropy.

glossary.def: Shannon's measure of uncertainty, in bits.
One yes or no answer; the unit of information.
The chess opening 1. d4 d5 2. c4.
An opening that gives up something to gain position.
A theme that returns again and again.
Latin: through hardship to the stars.

keyPoints: Shannon entropy is H = minus the sum of p times log p, over every outcome.
With logarithms base 2, entropy is measured in bits.
A fair coin has 1 bit; a coin that always lands heads has 0.
The Queen's Gambit is 1. d4 d5 2. c4: White offers the c-pawn.
Claude Shannon also wrote a famous 1950 paper on programming a computer to play chess.
Ingress, congress, egress: the Union is entering, meeting and leaving.

items: ELI5. Entropy is how many yes-or-no questions you need to guess what happens next. A chess opening is a first move that offers a small gift to win a bigger game.

The third image is just text, laid over a red picture of a woman's face. At the top, in square brackets, is a Latin motto, per aspera ad astra: through hardship to the stars. Below it is a formula, and then five lines, each marked with a Greek letter in brackets.

The first Greek letter is gamma, and the line is called Ingress, a way in. It holds the moves 1. d4 d5 2. c4. That is the Queen's Gambit. White pushes a pawn to the centre, Black answers, and White offers a second pawn, hoping to gain control of the centre.
If Black takes it, White usually wins it back.

Above the lines is the entropy formula, written in plain computer notation. Claude Shannon invented it in 1948 to measure information. If you do not know which of several things will happen, entropy says how many yes-or-no questions you would need on average to find out.

A fair coin has entropy 1 bit: one question settles it. A weighted coin that lands heads 90 percent of the time is less surprising and has about 0.47 bits. A coin that always lands heads has zero, because nothing is uncertain.
The math has moved from certainty in the first image to measured uncertainty here.
Chess fits. Shannon wrote about how a machine could play chess in 1950, and he estimated that the game has about ten to the power of 120 possible lines.

The last line of the image, Leitmotiv, quotes a chess novel, The Eight by Katherine Neville, about tactics and strategy: knowing what to do when there is something to do, and when there is nothing to do.

quiz.q: What does entropy measure?
What is the entropy of a coin that always lands heads?
Which moves are the Queen's Gambit?

chapters.title: The Union II: coordinates and congress

maps.title: Congress
links: Devils Tower | was | The first national monument
Close Encounters | ends | At the tower
First Key | begins | Ol sonf vorsg

summary: The second line, Coordinates, gives 44.5902 degrees north and 104.7146 degrees west. That is Devils Tower in Wyoming, a rock column that was the first United States national monument in 1906 and the place where the 1977 film Close Encounters of the Third Kind has its meeting with visitors.

The third line, Congress, quotes the opening words of the First Key of the Enochian language, which John Dee wrote down in the 1580s. Dee believed angels had given him the language through a partner who looked into a crystal.

keyPoints: A degree is 60 minutes and a minute is 60 seconds.
Devils Tower is at about 44.59 north, 104.71 west.
It became the first United States national monument in 1906.
Dee and his seer Edward Kelley recorded Enochian in the 1580s; the First Key is one of the Calls.

items: ELI5. Coordinates are the street address of a place on the whole Earth. A made-up language is like a secret handshake that only makes sense inside one story.

Coordinates are two numbers that say where something is. Latitude counts degrees north or south of the equator and longitude counts degrees east or west of the line through Greenwich. A degree can be split into 60 minutes, and each minute into 60 seconds, just like hours on a clock.

The numbers in the image, 44.5902 north and 104.7146 west, point to Devils Tower in northeast Wyoming. It is a tall column of rock which several Native nations hold sacred. In 1906 it became the first national monument in the United States.
In 1977 it appeared in a film about people meeting visitors from the sky, and in the film the tower is where the meeting takes place.
This is where the series says the devil gets closer. In the first image he was a drawing, in the second a story, and here he is a place you could visit.
The name Devils Tower is a mistranslation of a native name that meant something else, according to some accounts, which shows how names can make a place feel darker than it is.

The line Congress quotes the start of the First Key. John Dee was an English mathematician, navigator and adviser to Queen Elizabeth the First. In the 1580s he and a medium called Edward Kelley wrote down an angelic language in sessions with a crystal.
The opening words are usually translated as I reign over you, says the God of Justice.
Enochian has words, grammar and a script, and people still use it in ritual. Yet there is no evidence it is a language from outside, and linguists find that it behaves like English in disguise.
For the series it is one more language piled onto the pile, and its subject, a meeting between worlds, matches the word Congress.

practice.title: Degrees, minutes, seconds
practice.intro: Write to_dms(deg): deg is a non-negative decimal degree. Return [degrees, minutes, seconds] as three integers, with seconds rounded to the nearest whole second and carried over if the seconds reach 60.
practice.solution:
def to_dms(deg):
    d = int(deg)
    rest = (deg - d) * 60
    m = int(rest)
    s = int(round((rest - m) * 60))
    if s == 60:
        s = 0
        m += 1
    if m == 60:
        m = 0
        d += 1
    return [d, m, s]

practice.title: Distance between points
practice.intro: Write distance_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2): the great-circle distance in kilometres using the haversine formula with Earth radius 6371, rounded to 1 decimal.
practice.solution:
def distance_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
    import math
    k = math.pi / 180.0
    p1 = lat1 * k
    p2 = lat2 * k
    dp = (lat2 - lat1) * k
    dl = (lon2 - lon1) * k
    a = math.sin(dp / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dl / 2) ** 2
    return round(2 * 6371 * math.asin(math.sqrt(a)), 1)

chapters.title: The Union III: egress, the ephah and the owl

maps.title: Egress
links: Zechariah 5 | shows | A woman in a basket

summary: The fourth line, Egress, is Zechariah 5:6 in Hebrew, about the ephah, a measuring basket, that goes out. The verse says this is their eye in all the land. The Hebrew word for their eye, einam, contains the letter ayin again.

The last line of the image says in nomine Babalon, in the name of Babalon. Babalon is Aleister Crowley's spelling of Babylon, used for the Scarlet Woman of his religion, Thelema. The woman in the ephah is sent to Shinar, which is Babylon.
The five Greek letters on the labels spell glaux, owl.

glossary.def: A dry-measure basket in Zechariah's vision.
The Bible's name for the land of Babylon.
The old Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.
Crowley's spelling of Babylon, used for his Scarlet Woman.
Aleister Crowley's religion, founded in 1904.
Greek for owl, the bird of Athena.

keyPoints: In Zechariah 5:5 to 11 a woman called Wickedness sits in an ephah and is carried to Shinar.
The Hebrew in 5:6 reads einam, their eye; a few ancient versions read their iniquity, a one-letter difference.
Ayin is the first letter of einam: the same eye and circle.
Crowley's Babalon draws on the Whore of Babylon in Revelation 17.
The labels gamma, lambda, alpha, upsilon, xi spell glaux, owl.
Athena's owl stands for wisdom.

items: ELI5. Some letters hide a word when you read the first ones in order, like a spelled-out secret. A little verse about a basket is one place where one tiny letter changes the meaning.

Zechariah was a prophet of the sixth century before the common era, and chapter five is one of his night visions. He sees an ephah, a large measuring basket, going out through the land. A lead lid lifts and inside sits a woman, and the angel says her name is Wickedness.
The lid is pushed down again, and two women with the wings of a stork lift the basket and carry it away to Shinar, to build a house for it there.
The verse in the image comes just before the lid is lifted. The Hebrew reads: and he said, this is their eye in all the land. The word for their eye is einam, spelled ayin, yod, nun, mem.

Some ancient translations, including the Greek Septuagint, read instead their iniquity, avonam, spelled ayin, vav, nun, mem. Only one letter is different, a yod for a vav, and the two look alike in some scripts. Scholars debate which is original.

The series loves the eye reading, because it makes the third image a return to the letter ayin from the first. This is a good example of the lesson to come: a real textual variation has been used as a bridge, and the bridge is lovely, but it is the author's choice.

The last line, in nomine Babalon, borrows the phrase in the name of. Babalon is Aleister Crowley's spelling of Babylon. In Revelation 17 a woman rides a beast and is called Babylon the Great. Crowley turned her into a goddess of Thelema, his religion of 1904.
The woman in the ephah ends in Shinar, which is Babylon, so the series moves her in a ring from one Babylon to another.

Finally look at the Greek letters in brackets: gamma, lambda, alpha, upsilon, xi. Read in order they spell glaux, the Greek for owl. The owl belonged to Athena, goddess of wisdom, and Athena was called glaukopis, owl-eyed or bright-eyed.
The owl is a watching bird, and its name hides in the labels of the page.

chapters.title: The Creation I: the golem

maps.title: Golem
links: Adam | was | A golem at first
Maharal | is linked to | The legend

summary: The fourth image shows a small clay figure inside a square, with the letters gimel, lamed and mem on its chest. The Hebrew word golem first appears in Psalm 139:16 and means an unformed mass. The Talmud says Adam was a golem in his first hour.

In Sanhedrin 65b the sage Rava makes a man by means of a text, and another sage speaks to him. He does not answer, so the sage tells him to return to his dust. Later legends say a golem is brought to life by letters and stopped by erasing one.
The aleph of emet, truth, can be erased to make met, dead.

glossary.def: An unformed mass; later, a being made of clay and animated by letters.
The Talmud passage where Rava makes a man.
Book of Formation, an early text on creation through the letters.
One pairing of two letters of the 22; there are 231.
Abraham Abulafia, a 13th-century Kabbalist of letter combination.
Rabbi Judah Loew of Prague, 16th century.

keyPoints: Golem appears once in the Hebrew Bible, in Psalm 139:16, for an unformed substance.
Sanhedrin 65b: Rava makes a man who cannot speak and is told to return to dust.
Sefer Yetzirah describes creation through the 22 letters in 231 gates.
Abulafia taught a method of combining letters as a spiritual practice.
Emet minus its aleph is met, dead; the aleph is 1.
Linking the golem to the Maharal of Prague is a later legend; his own writings do not mention it.

items: ELI5. A golem is a person-shaped heap of clay that old stories say could be woken up with letters and put to sleep by rubbing one letter out, turning truth into dead.

The Hebrew word golem is rare. It occurs once in the Bible, in Psalm 139, where the poet says that God's eyes saw my golem, meaning my unformed substance before I had a shape. In the Talmud the word means something raw or unfinished.
Adam, in the first hour of his making, was a golem, a lump before the soul.

The Talmud, in Sanhedrin 65b, tells that the sage Rava created a man and sent him to Rabbi Zera. Zera spoke to the man and he did not answer. Zera said, you were made by one of the companions; return to your dust.
In the same passage two other sages study the Book of Formation every Friday and make a calf, and eat it. These are small, odd tales, not a legend of terror.

The Book of Formation, or Sefer Yetzirah, is an early Jewish text, of uncertain date, which says the world was made by thirty-two paths: ten numbers and twenty-two letters. It describes combining the letters in pairs, and counts the pairs: twenty-two letters make 231 gates.
This is where the idea of making by letter combination begins.
In the thirteenth century Abraham Abulafia turned the idea into a practice. He taught a science of combining letters, a kind of meditation on permutations.

Later stories, from the sixteenth century on, say that a golem is a clay figure given life by letters, with the word emet, truth, on its forehead. When the aleph is wiped out, the word becomes met, dead, and the golem turns to dust.

The famous golem of Prague belongs to the Maharal, Rabbi Judah Loew, who lived around 1520 to 1609. But the story attaches to him only in retellings from the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, and his own books do not mention it.
The oldest golem tales are quieter than the monster of the films. They are about the limits of human making.

chapters.title: The Creation II: grammar, language, machine

maps.title: GLM
links: Turing machine | has | Tape and states
Language model | is | A talking golem

summary: The fourth image has three formulas. G is a formal grammar, a set of symbols and rewriting rules. L is a language, the set of strings the grammar can produce. M is a Turing machine, the standard model of a computer. The labels G, L and M spell the Hebrew root of golem in the series' reading.
Noam Chomsky showed in 1956 that grammars come in levels, and that the most general level matches exactly what Turing machines can do. A grammar writes a language; a machine reads one.
The labs write strings from a grammar and run a small Turing machine.

glossary.def: G = (N, Sigma, P, S): nonterminals, terminals, rules and a start symbol.
A set of strings.
A tape, a head and a table of rules; the standard model of computation.
Four levels of grammar from regular to unrestricted.
A rule that rewrites one string as another.
To stop running.

keyPoints: A grammar is G = (N, Sigma, P, S): nonterminal symbols, terminals, productions and a start symbol.
A Turing machine is M = (Q, Gamma, b, Sigma, delta, q0, F): states, tape symbols, blank, input symbols, rules, start and accepting states.
The Chomsky hierarchy has four levels; the top level matches Turing machines.
Golem (גלם) is 3 + 30 + 40 = 73 in gematria, the same as wisdom (חכמה).
Oscar Schwartz's 2019 article in IEEE Spectrum traces language machines to Kabbalist letter-combination.
A language model, unlike the classic golem, does nothing but speak.

items: ELI5. A grammar is a recipe book for making sentences. A Turing machine is a tiny robot that follows a rule table on a long paper strip, and the two end up doing the same jobs.

Look at the three formulas around the golem. On the left, G. It is a formal grammar, a recipe for making strings. It has nonterminal symbols that can still be rewritten, terminal symbols that cannot, a set of rules, and a start symbol.
Starting with S and applying rules until only terminals remain makes a sentence of the language.

At the top, L. It is the language, the set of every string that the grammar can make. On the right, M. It is a Turing machine: a tape divided into cells, a head that reads and writes one cell at a time, a set of states, and a table of rules that say what to do next.
Alan Turing described it in 1936 as a model of what any computing can do.

The three are tied together. In 1956 Noam Chomsky ranked grammars in four levels. The simplest, regular grammars, match finite automata; context-free grammars match machines with a stack; and the most general grammars, with no restriction at all, match exactly the Turing machines.
So grammar, language and machine are three views of one idea.

Now the Hebrew. The three letters gimel, lamed and mem spell the root of golem, and the image's labels G, L and M echo them. In gematria the value is 3 plus 30 plus 40, which is 73, and so is chokhmah, wisdom.
The final mem, the closed form of the letter used at the end of a word, is a square, like the frame in the image, as the ring of ayin was a circle in the first.

The thesis of the series comes from an article by Oscar Schwartz in IEEE Spectrum in 2019. It argues that the idea of making language by rules goes back centuries before Turing, to the Kabbalists who combined letters. The classic golem could not speak.

A language model is a golem that does nothing but speak. This is the series' reading, and a vivid one, though people who study the history of computing will tell you the lines of descent are looser than a single story suggests.

chapters.title: Reading the series: signal and pattern

maps.title: Caveat
links: Birthday problem | shows | Coincidence is common

summary: The series connects an enormous number of things. Some links are in the sources: Exodus, Zechariah, Shannon, the Talmud, Legg and Hutter. Others were made by the person who saw them. The analysis itself says some may be pattern-finding, the trap of Foucault's Pendulum.
With forty ideas there are 780 possible pairs, so many matches are expected by chance. A good reader marks which links are in the sources and which are invented.
The conclusion of the series is a question.

glossary.def: Seeing meaning, like a face, in random patterns.
Seeing connections between unrelated things.
Surprisingly few people are needed for a shared birthday.
Noticing hits and forgetting misses.
A connection stated in the sources.
A connection made by the reader.

keyPoints: Ayin as circle and eye, the acrostics, Sanhedrin 65b and emet and met are in the sources or the text.
Reading I AM as a nontrivial loop, 73 equal to wisdom, and the square as final mem are interpretations.
N ideas give n times n minus 1 divided by 2 possible pairs.
In a room of 23 people the chance of a shared birthday is more than half.
Emet is 441, which is 21 squared, and Ehyeh is 21: a coincidence like those the series loves.
The series ends with a question: will the new golem become wisdom or run amok?

items: ELI5. If you hunt for patterns you will find plenty, even in noise. A careful reader asks which links are really in the books and which ones were added by the reader.
The analysis of this series closes with a confession. Some of these links may be pattern-finding, the author says, the very trap that Umberto Eco's Foucault's Pendulum warns about.

In that novel, three editors invent a grand conspiracy from a random list, and then the conspiracy starts to feel real. The quotation on the first image was chosen from that book, so the series carries its own warning.

Let us count. Suppose the series has forty distinct ideas: Ehyeh, ayin, Baphomet, the identity matrix, entropy, an owl, a golem and so on. The number of possible pairs is forty times thirty-nine, divided by two, which is 780. If even one in a hundred pairs seems to fit, you will find about eight.
Whether any of them is real depends on the evidence for each.
The birthday problem is the classic example. In a room of 23 people the chance that two share a birthday is just over one half. Coincidence is not rare; it is what a large number of pairs gives you.
Here is one from this very course: emet, truth, is 441 in gematria, and 441 is 21 squared, and Ehyeh is 21. That looks like a message. It is only arithmetic.

So read each link by type. Some are in the sources and can be checked: Exodus 3:14, the shape of ayin, the verse in Zechariah, Sanhedrin 65b, the Legg-Hutter formula, the Chomsky hierarchy, the article by Schwartz.
Some are the reader's: that the ring is also ayin, that I AM is a loop, that golem is wisdom, that a language model is a golem. Interpretation is not wrong, but it is not evidence.
In the end, the series says that the people who first dreamed of animating clay with letters and the people who now train machines on text are doing a related work.

Whether the new golem will grow into wisdom, as its number 73 hints, or into the rampaging servant of the Prague legend, the series does not say. That is arguably the question it asks. Now you have the tools to check each claim for yourself.
